summary: This bill amends the Small Business Act to require small business development centers and women’s business centers to educate small businesses on hiring graduates of career and technical education programs, inform those programs about center resources for starting businesses, and connect the two to identify job opportunities.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Small Business Act to add new informational and connective requirements for existing Small Business Development Centers and Women's Business Centers regarding career and technical education graduates. These centers receive federal funding, but the legislation does not authorize new appropriations, alter funding levels, or expand the scope of government spending. It merely modifies the duties of already-funded entities.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, coverage models, or medical services.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No references to immigration, visas, border policy, or pathways for foreign nationals.
The bill does not address reproductive health, abortion access, or related regulations.
No provisions involve military, defense, or national security spending or policy.
The bill makes no mention of environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation measures.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or other safety-net entitlements.

The bill references career and technical education (CTE) programs and requires small business centers to interact with them for workforce placement purposes. While this touches on education, it does not alter federal education funding, expand public school programs, promote school choice, or change education governance structures. The engagement is incidental to the primary small-business focus and does not advance either pole of the education topic.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-related regulations.
The legislation contains nothing related to sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions concern tariffs, trade agreements, import/export rules, or globalization policies.
The bill does not authorize new spending, create deficits, or include any debt-reduction mechanisms.
No provisions address legal protections, nondiscrimination rules, or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill has no connection to foreign assistance, international aid, or diplomatic spending.
No provisions relate to voting access, election administration, voter ID, or campaign finance.
The legislation does not address data privacy, technology regulation, or digital oversight.
While the bill encourages hiring from CTE programs, it contains no language on union rights, collective bargaining, worker protections, or employer flexibility regarding unions.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and antidiscrimination rules.
